questions.label: 1(a)(i)
questions.stem:
The function $\mathrm f$ is defined by $\mathrm f(x)=\dfrac{2x+1}{2x-1}$ for $x<\tfrac12$.

State the value of $\mathrm f(-1)$.

questions.label: 1(a)(ii)
questions.stem:
The function $\mathrm f$ is defined by $\mathrm f(x)=\dfrac{2x+1}{2x-1}$ for $x<\tfrac12$.

The diagram shows the graph of $y=\mathrm f(x)$. Sketch the graph of $y=\mathrm f^{-1}(x)$ on this diagram. Show any relevant mirror line.

figures.alt: Grid from −4 to 4 on both axes showing y = f(x) for x < ½: close to y = 1 on the far left, passing through (0, −1) and plunging downwards towards the asymptote x = ½.

questions.stem: The function $\mathrm g$ is defined by $\mathrm g(x)=\dfrac{2}{ax-3}+\dfrac12$ for $x>\dfrac3a$, where $a$ is a positive constant. Find $\mathrm g^{-1}(x)$ and hence verify that if $a=6$ then $\mathrm g^{-1}(x)\equiv\mathrm g(x)$.

questions.label: 3(a)
questions.stem:
The diagram shows the circle with equation $x^2+y^2-14x+8y+36=0$ and the line $y=-2$. The line intersects the circle at the points $A$ and $B$. The centre of the circle is $C$.

Find the coordinates of $A$, $B$ and $C$.

figures.alt: Circle with centre C below the x-axis, crossing the x-axis to the right of the y-axis; the horizontal line y = −2 cuts the circle at A (left) and B (right).

questions.label: 3(b)
questions.stem:
The diagram shows the circle with equation $x^2+y^2-14x+8y+36=0$ and the line $y=-2$. The line intersects the circle at the points $A$ and $B$. The centre of the circle is $C$.

Find the angle $ACB$ in radians. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

figures.alt: Circle with centre C below the x-axis, crossing the x-axis to the right of the y-axis; the horizontal line y = −2 cuts the circle at A (left) and B (right).

questions.label: 3(c)
questions.stem:
The diagram shows the circle with equation $x^2+y^2-14x+8y+36=0$ and the line $y=-2$. The line intersects the circle at the points $A$ and $B$. The centre of the circle is $C$. The chord $AB$ divides the circle into two segments.

Find the area of the larger segment.

figures.alt: Circle with centre C below the x-axis, crossing the x-axis to the right of the y-axis; the horizontal line y = −2 cuts the circle at A (left) and B (right).

questions.stem: Express $9x^2-36x+8$ in the form $p(x+q)^2+r$, where $p$, $q$ and $r$ are constants.

questions.label: 5(a)
questions.stem:
Functions $\mathrm f$ and $\mathrm g$ are defined as follows: $\mathrm f(x)=\dfrac{2x+1}{2x-1}$ for $x\ne\tfrac12$, and $\mathrm g(x)=x^2+4$ for $x\in\mathbb R$.

The diagram shows part of the graph of $y=\mathrm f(x)$. State the domain of $\mathrm f^{-1}$.

figures.alt: Graph of $y=(2x+1)/(2x-1)$ on a unit grid, x from -6 to 6 and y from -3 to 4. Axes are labelled x and y, with origin O. Two decreasing branches approach the asymptotes $x=1/2$ and $y=1$; the left branch crosses the axes at $(-1/2,0)$ and $(0,-1)$.

questions.label: 5(b)
questions.stem:
Functions $\mathrm f$ and $\mathrm g$ are defined as follows: $\mathrm f(x)=\dfrac{2x+1}{2x-1}$ for $x\ne\tfrac12$, and $\mathrm g(x)=x^2+4$ for $x\in\mathbb R$.

Find an expression for $\mathrm f^{-1}(x)$.

questions.label: 5(c)
questions.stem:
Functions $\mathrm f$ and $\mathrm g$ are defined as follows: $\mathrm f(x)=\dfrac{2x+1}{2x-1}$ for $x\ne\tfrac12$, and $\mathrm g(x)=x^2+4$ for $x\in\mathbb R$.

Find $\mathrm{gf}^{-1}(3)$.

questions.label: 5(d)
questions.stem:
Functions $\mathrm f$ and $\mathrm g$ are defined as follows: $\mathrm f(x)=\dfrac{2x+1}{2x-1}$ for $x\ne\tfrac12$, and $\mathrm g(x)=x^2+4$ for $x\in\mathbb R$.

Explain why $\mathrm g^{-1}(x)$ cannot be found.

The diagram shows a sector $OAB$ of a circle with centre $O$. Angle $AOB=\theta$ radians and $OP=AP=x$.

Show that the arc length $AB$ is $2x\theta\cos\theta$.

figures.alt: Sector $OAB$ with centre $O$ on the left; $OB$ is horizontal and $B$ is on the right. $A$ is above the line $OB$ on the arc. The point $P$ lies on $OB$ with $OP=AP=x$. Angle $AOB=\theta$ rad is marked at $O$. The shaded region is bounded by $AP$, $PB$ and the arc $AB$.

questions.label: 7(a)
questions.stem:
A circle with centre $C$ has equation $(x-8)^2+(y-4)^2=100$.

Show that the point $T(-6,\,6)$ is outside the circle.

questions.label: 7(b)
questions.stem:
A circle with centre $C$ has equation $(x-8)^2+(y-4)^2=100$. Two tangents from the point $T(-6,\,6)$ to the circle are drawn.

Show that the angle between one of the tangents and $CT$ is exactly $45^\circ$.

questions.label: 7(c)
questions.stem:
A circle with centre $C$ has equation $(x-8)^2+(y-4)^2=100$. Two tangents from the point $T(-6,\,6)$ to the circle are drawn. The two tangents touch the circle at $A$ and $B$.

Find the equation of the line $AB$, giving your answer in the form $y=mx+c$.

questions.label: 7(d)
questions.stem:
A circle with centre $C$ has equation $(x-8)^2+(y-4)^2=100$. Two tangents from the point $T(-6,\,6)$ to the circle are drawn. The two tangents touch the circle at $A$ and $B$.

Find the $x$-coordinates of $A$ and $B$.

questions.label: 8(a)
questions.stem:
The diagram shows a cross-section $RASB$ of the body of an aircraft. The cross-section consists of a sector $OARB$ of a circle of radius $2.5\ \mathrm m$, with centre $O$, a sector $PASB$ of another circle of radius $2.24\ \mathrm m$ with centre $P$ and a quadrilateral $OAPB$. Angle $AOB=\tfrac23\pi$ and angle $APB=\tfrac56\pi$.

Find the perimeter of the cross-section $RASB$, giving your answer correct to 2 decimal places.

figures.alt: Aircraft cross-section RASB. A and B lie on a horizontal chord, R on the top major arc of a circle centred at O, S on the lower arc of a circle centred at P; O is above P and both lie above AB. Dashed OA=OB=2.5 m and PA=PB=2.24 m. Angles AOB=2π/3 and APB=5π/6 point downward. The boundary is the major arc ARB and minor arc ASB; quadrilateral OAPB fills the space between the two sectors.

questions.label: 8(b)
questions.stem:
The diagram shows a cross-section $RASB$ of the body of an aircraft. The cross-section consists of a sector $OARB$ of a circle of radius $2.5\ \mathrm m$, with centre $O$, a sector $PASB$ of another circle of radius $2.24\ \mathrm m$ with centre $P$ and a quadrilateral $OAPB$. Angle $AOB=\tfrac23\pi$ and angle $APB=\tfrac56\pi$.

Find the difference in area of the two triangles $AOB$ and $APB$, giving your answer correct to 2 decimal places.

figures.alt: Aircraft cross-section RASB. A and B lie on a horizontal chord, R on the top major arc of a circle centred at O, S on the lower arc of a circle centred at P; O is above P and both lie above AB. Dashed OA=OB=2.5 m and PA=PB=2.24 m. Angles AOB=2π/3 and APB=5π/6 point downward. The boundary is the major arc ARB and minor arc ASB; quadrilateral OAPB fills the space between the two sectors.

questions.label: 8(c)
questions.stem:
The diagram shows a cross-section $RASB$ of the body of an aircraft. The cross-section consists of a sector $OARB$ of a circle of radius $2.5\ \mathrm m$, with centre $O$, a sector $PASB$ of another circle of radius $2.24\ \mathrm m$ with centre $P$ and a quadrilateral $OAPB$. Angle $AOB=\tfrac23\pi$ and angle $APB=\tfrac56\pi$.

Find the area of the cross-section $RASB$, giving your answer correct to 1 decimal place.

figures.alt: Aircraft cross-section RASB. A and B lie on a horizontal chord, R on the top major arc of a circle centred at O, S on the lower arc of a circle centred at P; O is above P and both lie above AB. Dashed OA=OB=2.5 m and PA=PB=2.24 m. Angles AOB=2π/3 and APB=5π/6 point downward. The boundary is the major arc ARB and minor arc ASB; quadrilateral OAPB fills the space between the two sectors.

questions.label: 9(a)
questions.stem:
The equation of a circle is $x^2+y^2+ax+by-12=0$. The points $A(1,1)$ and $B(2,-6)$ lie on the circle.

Find the values of $a$ and $b$ and hence find the coordinates of the centre of the circle.

questions.label: 9(b)
questions.stem:
The equation of a circle is $x^2+y^2+ax+by-12=0$. The points $A(1,1)$ and $B(2,-6)$ lie on the circle.

Find the equation of the tangent to the circle at the point $A$, giving your answer in the form $px+qy=k$, where $p$, $q$ and $k$ are integers.

questions.label: 10(a)
questions.stem:
The function $\mathrm f$ is defined by $\mathrm f(x)=\dfrac{2x}{3x-1}$ for $x>\tfrac13$.

Find an expression for $\mathrm f^{-1}(x)$.

questions.label: 10(b)
questions.stem:
The function $\mathrm f$ is defined by $\mathrm f(x)=\dfrac{2x}{3x-1}$ for $x>\tfrac13$.

Show that $\dfrac23+\dfrac{2}{3(3x-1)}$ can be expressed as $\dfrac{2x}{3x-1}$.

questions.label: 11(a)
questions.stem:
In the diagram, the graph with equation $y=\mathrm f(x)$ is shown with solid lines and the graph with equation $y=\mathrm g(x)$ is shown with broken lines.

Describe fully a sequence of three transformations which transforms the graph of $y=\mathrm f(x)$ to the graph of $y=\mathrm g(x)$.

figures.alt: Grid, x from −6 to 4, y from 0 to 6. Solid y = f(x): straight segments (0, 3)→(1, 1)→(2, 1)→(4, 2). Broken y = g(x): (−5, 4)→(−3, 2)→(−2, 2)→(−1, 6).

questions.label: 11(b)
questions.stem:
In the diagram, the graph with equation $y=\mathrm f(x)$ is shown with solid lines and the graph with equation $y=\mathrm g(x)$ is shown with broken lines.

Find an expression for $\mathrm g(x)$ in the form $a\mathrm f(bx+c)$, where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are integers.

figures.alt: Grid, x from −6 to 4, y from 0 to 6. Solid y = f(x): straight segments (0, 3)→(1, 1)→(2, 1)→(4, 2). Broken y = g(x): (−5, 4)→(−3, 2)→(−2, 2)→(−1, 6).

questions.label: 12(a)
questions.stem:
The functions $\mathrm f$ and $\mathrm g$ are defined by $$\mathrm f(x)=\sqrt x\ \text{ for }x\geqslant0,\qquad\mathrm g(x)=3\sqrt{x+2}-5\ \text{ for }x\geqslant-2.$$

Describe fully a sequence of transformations which transforms the graph of $y=\mathrm f(x)$ to the graph of $y=\mathrm g(x)$. You should make clear the order in which the transformations are applied.

questions.label: 12(b)
questions.stem:
The functions $\mathrm f$ and $\mathrm g$ are defined by $$\mathrm f(x)=\sqrt x\ \text{ for }x\geqslant0,\qquad\mathrm g(x)=3\sqrt{x+2}-5\ \text{ for }x\geqslant-2.$$ The diagram shows the graph of $y=\mathrm g(x)$.

On the diagram sketch the graph of $y=\mathrm g^{-1}(x)$ together with any relevant mirror line.

figures.alt: Axes with origin O. The curve y = g(x) starts below the x-axis at the lower left (at (−2, −5)), cuts the y-axis below O, crosses the x-axis to the right of O and rises slowly to the upper right.

questions.label: 12(c)
questions.stem:
The functions $\mathrm f$ and $\mathrm g$ are defined by $$\mathrm f(x)=\sqrt x\ \text{ for }x\geqslant0,\qquad\mathrm g(x)=3\sqrt{x+2}-5\ \text{ for }x\geqslant-2.$$

Find an expression for $\mathrm g^{-1}(x)$.

questions.label: 12(d)
questions.stem:
The functions $\mathrm f$ and $\mathrm g$ are defined by $$\mathrm f(x)=\sqrt x\ \text{ for }x\geqslant0,\qquad\mathrm g(x)=3\sqrt{x+2}-5\ \text{ for }x\geqslant-2.$$

State the range of $\mathrm g^{-1}$.

The diagram shows a triangle $ABC$, in which angle $ABC=90^\circ$ and $AB=4$ cm. The sector $ABD$ is part of a circle with centre $A$. The area of the sector is $10\ \mathrm{cm}^2$.

Find angle $BAD$ in radians.

figures.alt: Right triangle ABC, right angle at B, vertical AB = 4 cm. D lies on AC, AD = AB = 4 cm. Arc BD is centred at A. Region BCD, outside sector ABD and inside triangle ABC, is shaded.

questions.stem:
The diagram shows the graphs of $y=x^3$ and $y=\mathrm f(x)$. The graph of $y=x^3$ is transformed to the graph of $y=\mathrm f(x)$ by a sequence of transformations.

Describe fully a suitable sequence of transformations. Make clear the order in which the transformations are applied.

figures.alt: Grid from x = −1 to 5 and y = −8 to 6. The curve y = x³ passes through (−1, −1), (0, 0), (1, 1). The curve y = f(x) is the same shape, steeper, with its point of inflection at (3, −4); it passes through about (2, −6) and (4, −2).

questions.label: 15(a)
questions.stem:
Functions $\mathrm f$, $\mathrm g$ and $\mathrm h$ are defined as follows: $\mathrm f:x\mapsto x-4x^{1/2}+1$ for $x\geqslant0$; $\mathrm g:x\mapsto mx^2+n$ for $x\geqslant-2$, where $m$ and $n$ are constants; $\mathrm h:x\mapsto x^{1/2}-2$ for $x\geqslant0$.

Solve the equation $\mathrm f(x)=0$, giving your solutions in the form $x=a+b\sqrt c$, where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are integers.

questions.label: 15(b)
questions.stem:
Functions $\mathrm f$, $\mathrm g$ and $\mathrm h$ are defined as follows: $\mathrm f:x\mapsto x-4x^{1/2}+1$ for $x\geqslant0$; $\mathrm g:x\mapsto mx^2+n$ for $x\geqslant-2$, where $m$ and $n$ are constants; $\mathrm h:x\mapsto x^{1/2}-2$ for $x\geqslant0$.

Given that $\mathrm f(x)\equiv\mathrm{gh}(x)$, find the values of $m$ and $n$.

questions.label: 16(a)
questions.stem:
The functions $\mathrm f$ and $\mathrm g$ are defined as follows, where $a$ and $b$ are constants.
$\mathrm f(x)=1+\dfrac{2a}{x-a}\ \text{ for }x>a$
$\mathrm g(x)=bx-2\ \text{ for }x\in\mathbb R$ Given that $\mathrm f(7)=\tfrac52$ and $\mathrm{gf}(5)=4$, find the values of $a$ and $b$.

questions.label: 16(b)
questions.stem:
The functions $\mathrm f$ and $\mathrm g$ are defined as follows, where $a$ and $b$ are constants.
$\mathrm f(x)=1+\dfrac{2a}{x-a}\ \text{ for }x>a$
$\mathrm g(x)=bx-2\ \text{ for }x\in\mathbb R$ For the rest of this question, you should use the value of $a$ which you found in (a). Find the domain of $\mathrm f^{-1}$.

questions.label: 16(c)
questions.stem:
The functions $\mathrm f$ and $\mathrm g$ are defined as follows, where $a$ and $b$ are constants.
$\mathrm f(x)=1+\dfrac{2a}{x-a}\ \text{ for }x>a$
$\mathrm g(x)=bx-2\ \text{ for }x\in\mathbb R$ For the rest of this question, you should use the value of $a$ which you found in (a). Find an expression for $\mathrm f^{-1}(x)$.

questions.label: 17(a)
questions.stem:
The diagram shows the graph of $y=\mathrm f(x)$ where the function $\mathrm f$ is defined by $\mathrm f(x)=3+2\sin\tfrac14x$ for $0\leqslant x\leqslant2\pi$.

On the diagram above, sketch the graph of $y=\mathrm f^{-1}(x)$.

figures.alt: Grid for sketching. The $x$-axis is marked at $-\tfrac52\pi$, $-2\pi$, $-\tfrac32\pi$, $-\pi$, $-\tfrac12\pi$, $0$, $\tfrac12\pi$, $\pi$, $\tfrac32\pi$, $2\pi$, $\tfrac52\pi$ (two grid squares per $\tfrac12\pi$); the $y$-axis is marked at $\tfrac12\pi$, $\pi$, $\tfrac32\pi$, $2\pi$. The curve drawn runs from $(0,3)$ (just below $\pi$ on the $y$-axis) rising and bending over (concave down) to $(2\pi,5)$ (just above $\tfrac32\pi$). Nothing is drawn for $x<0$.

questions.label: 17(b)
questions.stem:
The diagram shows the graph of $y=\mathrm f(x)$ where the function $\mathrm f$ is defined by $\mathrm f(x)=3+2\sin\tfrac14x$ for $0\leqslant x\leqslant2\pi$.

Find an expression for $\mathrm f^{-1}(x)$.

questions.label: 17(c)
questions.stem:
The diagram shows the graph of $y=\mathrm f(x)$ where the function $\mathrm f$ is defined by $\mathrm f(x)=3+2\sin\tfrac14x$ for $0\leqslant x\leqslant2\pi$. The diagram above shows part of the graph of the function $\mathrm g(x)=3+2\sin\tfrac14x$ for $-2\pi\leqslant x\leqslant2\pi$.

Complete the sketch of the graph of $\mathrm g(x)$ on the diagram above and hence explain whether the function $\mathrm g$ has an inverse.

figures.alt: Grid for sketching. The $x$-axis is marked at $-\tfrac52\pi$, $-2\pi$, $-\tfrac32\pi$, $-\pi$, $-\tfrac12\pi$, $0$, $\tfrac12\pi$, $\pi$, $\tfrac32\pi$, $2\pi$, $\tfrac52\pi$ (two grid squares per $\tfrac12\pi$); the $y$-axis is marked at $\tfrac12\pi$, $\pi$, $\tfrac32\pi$, $2\pi$. The curve drawn runs from $(0,3)$ (just below $\pi$ on the $y$-axis) rising and bending over (concave down) to $(2\pi,5)$ (just above $\tfrac32\pi$). Nothing is drawn for $x<0$.

questions.stem: Express $x^2+6x+5$ in the form $(x+a)^2+b$, where $a$ and $b$ are constants.

The diagram shows the circle with equation $x^2+y^2=20$. Tangents touching the circle at points $B$ and $C$ pass through the point $A(0,10)$.

By letting the equation of a tangent be $y=mx+10$, find the two possible values of $m$.

figures.alt: Circle x² + y² = 20 centred at origin O, with x- and y-axes. A(0,10) is above the circle. Tangents AB and AC touch the upper-left and upper-right of the circle at B and C respectively. D is the intersection of the circle with the positive x-axis.

questions.label: 20(a)
questions.stem: Express $2x^2-8x+14$ in the form $2[(x-a)^2+b]$.

questions.label: 20(b)
questions.stem:
The functions $\mathrm f$ and $\mathrm g$ are defined by $\mathrm f(x)=x^2$ for $x\in\mathbb R$, $\mathrm g(x)=2x^2-8x+14$ for $x\in\mathbb R$.

Describe fully a sequence of transformations that maps the graph of $y=\mathrm f(x)$ onto the graph of $y=\mathrm g(x)$, making clear the order in which the transformations are applied.
